finalText:
Two things usually cause this.

First, a normal component re-renders whenever its parent re-renders, no matter what the props are. Wrapping it in `React.memo` is what makes React actually compare the props and skip the re-render if they look the same.

Second, even with `React.memo`, it still won't help if you're passing a new function or object each time — like an inline `() => ...}` or `{ foo: 1 }` written straight in the parent's return. Those look "the same" to you but are a brand new value every render, so the comparison always fails. Wrap those in `useCallback` or `useMemo` in the parent so the same reference gets reused.

If you share the parent and child code, I can point at the exact spot causing it.
